title: Transient reserve starvation during autoscaler reconfiguration affecting burst allocations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A subset of customers experienced sudden request throttling and burst credit exhaustion during a regional autoscaler leader reconfiguration (control-plane maintenance). The problem manifested as transient reserve pool starvation for affected tenants for 2–8 minutes, causing elevated 429/503 rates and customer escalations from three mid-market tenants.

Timeline of events:
- 2026-03-09 22:07 UTC: rolling leader re-election started in region us-west-2 for the autoscaler control plane as part of maintenance.
- 2026-03-09 22:09 UTC: first customer report from AcmeHealth showing increased latency and 429s.
- 2026-03-09 22:10–22:16 UTC: multiple tenants observed sudden drop in reserved pool headroom despite normal add/remove events.
- 2026-03-09 22:20 UTC: on-call identified burst ledger counter reaching zero for impacted tenants; autoscaler metrics showed short-lived double-decrement events on commit path.

Root cause hypothesis and evidence:
- The autoscaler controller executes a two-phase reconciliation when processing lease table updates. During a leader reconfiguration window, one of the commit paths retried a reconciliation with stale in-memory delta, causing an idempotency violation that double-applied a debit to tenant burst-credit ledgers.
- Postmortem telemetry: correlating request traces to lease-commit events shows duplicate reconcile commits from controller instances that thought they were the leader due to a 3-second timing gap in the leader-election grace window.
- The double-debit only affected tenants whose weight and affinity placed them on cross-az reserved pools where the reconciliation path uses optimistic in-memory aggregation before persisting. This exposed a race between in-memory aggregation rollback and the persisted ledger write.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- At 22:30 UTC we rolled a hotfix to the autoscaler service that gated leader-only reconciliation behind a tombstone check and added a short mutual-exclusion backoff for commit windows. That reduced duplicate commits and allowed most affected tenants to recover headroom within 4–10 minutes.
- We executed a targeted compensating re-credit for fully identified tenants (runbook link below) to restore lost burst credits where automated recovery had not completed.

Customer communications:
- Customer success notified the three escalated accounts and provided status updates and recovery timeline. Template used: https://confluence.redwood.example.com/display/CS/Reserved+Pool+Starvation+Escalation+Template
- Post-recovery we scheduled follow-ups with impacted customers to validate application health and confirm no downstream regressions.

Planned permanent fixes and trade-offs considered:
1) Idempotent commit protocol: introduce a server-side deduplication key for reconciliation writes so retries cannot double-apply. Trade-off: requires schema bump and careful migration for older ledger rows. Estimated effort: 5 points.
2) Leader-election grace extension: increase the grace window to avoid overlapping leader perceptions. Trade-off: slightly longer failover time during genuine leader loss; may delay scale decisions in tight failure modes. Estimated effort: 2 points.
3) Replace optimistic in-memory aggregation with immediate durable prepare step: eliminates the in-memory rollback race. Trade-off: small latency increase on reconciliation hot path; complexity in refactoring. Estimated effort: 8 points.

Decisions so far:
- Implement (1) idempotent commit protocol as highest priority to make reconciliations safe under retries.
- Implement (2) as a short-term operational guard in the next release to reduce likelihood of overlapping leadership windows.
- Defer (3) for now; instrument aggregation paths and evaluate performance impact in a canary before committing to the change.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Create unit and integration tests that simulate leader flip with concurrent reconcile attempts.
- Canary rollout to a non-production region and then to us-west-2 with 10% traffic for 2 hours before full rollout.
- Monitor new telemetry flags: reconcile_duplicate_count, ledger_recovery_actions, and per-tenant burst delta anomalies.

Artifacts and links:
- Debug dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.example.com/d/saas/autoscaler-lease-telemetry?orgId=1
- Runbook for compensating re-credit: https://confluence.redwood.example.com/display/Runbooks/Compensating+Burst+Recredit
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/9721
- Planned ipd PR for durable dedupe: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/9802

Post-incident actions and owners:
- ENG-325468: develop and ship idempotent commit (assignee: Marco Hernandez). Due 2026-03-18.
- Add reconcile_duplicate_count to prod metrics (owner: Priya Sen). Due 2026-03-14.
- Prepare customer-facing postmortem and send to CS (owner: Aisha Patel). Due 2026-03-15.

Open questions:
- Should we also apply a one-time sweep across all tenants to detect and auto-repair small unexplained negative deltas? Risk of masking other bugs vs improving customer experience.
- If we extend leader-election grace windows, what SLA tradeoffs are acceptable for large customers? Need PM guidance.
